correctness.rationale: The spatial pairing yields z=δH+C cosθ+iS sinθ exactly. On (0,1), B=|S| has a unique nondegenerate maximum by strict monotonicity of its derivative polynomial-like function D_p. This establishes all top-height maximizers and a symmetric missing midpoint for any nonzero δ. The real-zero constraint yields a one-variable objective with small-δ maximizers displaced only O_p(δ²), giving the exact positive quadratic coefficient, and its equal-modulus rescaling yields the strong-split asymptotic. For p=4, k=(1-t²)/(1+t²) reduces the axial squared height to u[1-(1+4δ²)u]/(1+u)²; its unique critical point gives the exact global maximum and explicit witnesses. All boundary cases, p=2 and δ=0, are handled. Python standard-library diagnostic checks 2246 finite instances; it is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural geometric stability problem: how much the distinguished vertical chord of a known convex quartic Banach-space numerical range is lost upon a real diagonal split. The exact, all-split quartic height and extremizers quantify the full nonlinear transition, while the sharp general-p quadratic onset and large-split rate identify universal analytic regimes. The numerical quantities are intrinsically tied to the midpoint nonconvexity witness rather than arbitrary slices. The results add quantitative information not implied by the earlier qualitative nonconvexity theorem or zero-split area formula.
